topic: The only Docker commands you need to get started
angle: A complete beginner workflow for one disposable practice container: run, inspect with ps and logs, stop, then remove. Scope the minimum set to this first-container exercise, not all Docker work.
audience: Beginners who have Docker installed and running and want their first useful terminal workflow

sources.title: Docker container run
sources.excerpt: docker run creates and starts a new container from an image, pulling the image when it is missing. --name assigns a custom container name. -d runs it in the background. The documented example is docker run --name test -d nginx:alpine. The same name can be used in later commands. Changing test to demo is an illustrative chosen name.

sources.title: Docker container ls
sources.excerpt: docker ps is an alias for docker container ls. It lists running containers by default; docker ps -a also includes stopped containers. Output includes image, status and name.

sources.title: Docker container logs
sources.excerpt: docker logs CONTAINER retrieves the logs present at execution time. The command displays the container standard output and standard error; --follow streams new output. The illustrative command docker logs demo reads the named practice container logs.

sources.title: Docker container stop
sources.excerpt: docker stop CONTAINER stops a running container. The main process receives a termination signal, followed by a kill signal if it does not exit in the timeout. docker stop demo stops the named practice container. A stopped container still exists.

sources.title: Docker container rm
sources.excerpt: docker rm CONTAINER removes containers. Stop a running container before ordinary removal; the documentation demonstrates docker stop test followed by docker rm test. docker rm demo removes the stopped practice container. It does not remove the image; deleting a container discards its writable layer, so this demonstration is for a disposable practice container.

notes: Write 100–115 spoken words for a brisk but clear 40–50 second Short, using six sections.
Use exactly this display sequence: docker run --name demo -d nginx:alpine; docker ps; docker logs demo; docker stop demo; docker rm demo. Keep demo consistent.

Start with an immediate specific hook, then mention Docker already installed. Explain run creates/starts, -d means background, ps checks running, logs reads output, stop stops and rm removes the stopped practice container.
Do not claim a published web page: no ports are exposed in this exercise. Do not add pull, exec, build, compose or unrelated commands.
Spoken narration should explain meaning rather than dictate every punctuation mark. Put exact commands in scene visual elements. Make the viewer able to follow the workflow visually.
Keep the final viewer ask brief and useful: save or try this on a practice container. Avoid a generic channel pitch.
Visuals will use large animated terminal text and explicit running/stopped/removed state cards. On-screen terminal output must be identified as edited or abbreviated if not exact captured output.

Creative revision after attempt one: the rhetorical question opening and 127 words felt formal and padded. Use a direct punchy hook, not a how-do-you question. Suggested direction: Stop memorizing Docker commands—run your first container with these five. Keep a hook candidate that the first sentence matches exactly.

Target 105–115 spoken words. Cut phrases such as when you are finished inspecting it, standard output and standard error already recorded, and that is the full first-container workflow. Explain logs as what the app prints.
Keep Docker installed/running as a concise prerequisite on screen, not a long spoken setup. Name the container demo. End with one short save-this-workflow ask.
